title: Much Sharper Than a Serpents Tooth

contact_edits.before: So the last scene of newlywed squabbles, graced also by a promising Nerissa from Raquel Duffy, packs an unusual and many- layered punch. A final attempt to draw all the threads together, though, overreaches itself. Sara Topham's excellent Jessica ends the play fearful and alone, with a Hebrew hymn reproaching her over the sound system. Directors are always trying to read these regrets into the Jew's renegade daughter, and one can understand why, but there's no textual evidence for them. I hate to say it, but Shakespeare's Jessica seems perfectly happy among all those rich and lucky Christians. - In repertoire through Oct. 27. Call 1-800-567-1600 for details.
